entries.title: Micah 7:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Woe is me - The land is brought in complaining, that whereas it was once well stored, now it hath few good in it. As the grape - gleanings - In Israel and Judah, which in bringing forth good men, should have been a fruitful vine full of clusters: just, compassionate and humble men, are as grapes after the vintage is gathered. Desired - But in vain.

entries.title: Micah 7:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Both hands - With all diligence. The great man - The great man at court, who can do what he will there. Uttereth - Is bold to speak plainly. Desire - His unjust, oppressive design. They - They all jointly promote violence and cruelty.

entries.title: Micah 7:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: As a briar - Mischievous and hurtful. The day - The day in which they shall sound the alarm. Cometh - Surely, speedily, and unavoidably. Now - When that day is come.

entries.title: Micah 7:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Therefore - Since all sorts of men are so perfidious. Look - As one set in a watch - tower looks round about, and diligently observes all that stirs, so will the prophet; so did they who in Israel and Judah feared the Lord.

entries.title: Micah 7:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rejoice not - The prophet personates the church. Let it be no matter of glorying to thee, that the day of calamity hath overtaken me. In darkness - When affliction, war, famine, and captivity cover me. A light - Shall support, comfort and deliver me.

entries.title: Micah 7:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Plead - Against mine enemy, now he pleads his own cause against me. His righteousness - The truth and riches of his promised salvation.

entries.title: Micah 7:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: She - What nation or people soever. Shall behold - The people of God shall see their enemies laid low.

entries.title: Micah 7:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thy walls - O Jerusalem. The decree - Of Artaxerxes, which forbad the re - building of the temple. Removed - Abolished.

entries.title: Micah 7:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In that day - After the return out of captivity. He - He who is of Jewish race. To thee - O Jerusalem. The fortified cities - In which many Jews were kept for servile works. To the river - To Euphrates. To sea - From the Caspian to the Persian and to the Midland sea. From mountain - That is, from all parts of their captivity, they shall return to their own country.

entries.title: Micah 7:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not withstanding - These promises of restitution, which took not place 'till more than two hundred years after.

entries.title: Micah 7:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Feed - So Christ directs his officers. With thy rod - In allusion to the custom of shepherds who guided their sheep by a pastoral staff. In the wood - Protect and guide those that in their present captive state are solitary, compassed with dangers. Carmel - A fruitful place and well inhabited. In Bashan - A place of note for fruitfulness. Gilead - Equal with any of the other for plenty and safety.

entries.title: Micah 7:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Shall be deaf - They shall neither care to hear, nor to speak of it.

entries.title: Micah 7:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lick the dust - In the most submissive, servile manner, testify their subjection. Holes - Their strong holds, and fastnesses. Because of thee - So that the name of Jews, shall be terrible to their enemies.
